question: How do coalescing, vectorized access, shared-memory tiling, bank-conflict avoidance, read-only caches and TMA prefetching change GPU kernel memory behaviour, and how are they profiled?
contributions: Before/after CUDA C++ and PyTorch examples for six memory-access techniques with Nsight Compute metric tables

limits: All metrics tables are labelled illustrative; real benchmarks are in the book's GitHub repository.
GPU model, CUDA version, clocks and run counts for the tables are not stated.
Several table values are internally inconsistent (31.8 sectors/request for a scalar copy; 90% of peak DRAM at 10 GB/s).
Examples use FP32 CUDA cores, not Tensor Cores (Chapter 9 covers reduced precision).
Host-device overlap with pinned memory and streams appears only as a takeaway, with no example or numbers.
practices: Index so a warp's threads read consecutive 4-byte words, or use SoA, to coalesce (Coalesced section).
Use float4 (16 B) vectors, or 32 B aligned types on Blackwell with CUDA 13+, and keep pointers aligned (Vectorized section).
Tile 32x32 into shared memory for reuse; experiment with tile size against shared memory and register budgets (Tiling section).
Pad shared tiles to [32][33] or swizzle to avoid bank conflicts (Bank-conflict section).
Use __shfl_down_sync for intra-warp reductions instead of shared memory (Warp shuffle section).
Mark read-only data const __restrict__ (Read-only cache section).
Use cuda::memcpy_async with cuda::pipeline and double buffering so TMA overlaps copy with compute (TMA section).
Allocate pinned host memory and use cudaMemcpyAsync on multiple streams (Key Takeaways).
Profile with Nsight Compute and Nsight Systems before and after each change (Key Takeaways).

terms.definition: Coalescing is achieved when each warp's accesses fall within as few 128-byte cache lines as possible.
If multiple threads in a warp access the same bank, a bank conflict occurs. This forces the memory accesses to serialize
Swizzling is a compile-time index transformation that "scrambles" the linear index used for shared memory so that sequential threads map to different banks.
While TMA streams in the next tile of data, the SM's warps compute on the previous tile (ping-ponging).
